comments.author: @JosuaKrause
comments.text: Janus refers to unintentionally creating two-headed entities (the two headed polar bear for example). This comes from the training data which primarily has shots from the front of objects but fewer from behind. So the model doesn't really know how a polar bear looks from behind so it just uses the front again. That's also why the magician in the video, when he turns around, has another face at the back of his head. It's fitting in the context of the video but it is a limitation.

comments.author: @tiagotiagot
comments.text: I think the Janus issue is exactly the opposite you described; extra heads showing when they shouldn't. Similar issue is present with some text to 3d model creators; the face/head is such an important element that during rotations the model just adds another one because it was trained on it almost always being visible. My guess is they're probably generating things more sequentially than as a whole. I imagine it might've been better if they had trained with the video frames stacked and rotated so time is one of the spatial axis and vice-versa; or maybe even a combo of regular sequential and rotated, or even throwing random space-time rotations and not just 90 degrees, to really give it a grasp of how things fit in all possible ways (obviously to output the final result, the rotation needs to be undone to render the final normal video output correctly).

comments.author: @Sheblah1
comments.text:
The only obstacle to better quality AI image/movie/music production is lack of more data. AI improves in consistency with more data and that's going to take time. Not because it takes time to get and clean it (though it all adds up) but because AI companies have to work out how to hop, skip, and jump as fast as they quasi-legally can across a moral minefield - that goes on and on as far as the ai can see - just to stay ahead of the game. The mathematics was always there and the tech supply is at worst minimally bottlenecked and at best untramelled. It's a megamonstrous glut of fresh data that's needed. And as always it must come in the form of other people's work. I don't say this to stir up more outrage. 

Most of the good clips look like they've been trained on stock footage and 'ahem' trailers. I could be wrong. I personally think the way forward is to adopt the tech and use it skillfully as human skill will still be needed to produce masterpieces in all fields of creative endeavour. My opinion of course but hey enough of my yap, what d'you say, let's rock 🎸🎸
